topArticle.title: Fears grow that US will put Nobel-winning judge under sanctions after Myanmar genocide ruling
topArticle.description:
A ruling against Myanmar could set precedent for court’s judgment on Israel’s actions in Gaza
Fears are growing that the US could impose sanctions on judges at the international court of justice, including this year’s Nobel peace prize winner, Navi Pillay, if the court rules on Thursday that the Myanmar government committed genocide against the Rohingya.
The ICJ has never found a state responsible for committing genocide, and a significant factor in previous cases has been how to prove “intent” in a crime defined as acts committed with the “intent to destroy, in whole or in part” a national, ethnical, racial or religious group.

Leaked documents raise questions about claims Egypt met welfare targets to qualify for €2.5bn in loans
The European Commission has been accused of sugarcoating figures to enable it to release funds to Egypt under a landmark pact with the authoritarian government of Abdel Fatah al-Sisi.
The charge relates to a €7.4bn deal promised by Ursula von der Leyen, the European Commission president, to al-Sisi on a high-profile visit to Cairo in 2024. The three-year “strategic and comprehensive partnership” was intended to bolster Egypt’s shaky economy, deter migrants from coming to Europe and shore up a region reeling from the 7 October attacks and Israel’s war on Gaza.

topArticle.title: Ireland contributes EUR 200,000 to strengthen trade opportunities in developing countries
topArticle.description: Ireland is contributing EUR 200,000 (approximately CHF 185,000) to the Standards and Trade Development Facility (STDF) in 2026 to strengthen sanitary and phytosanitary capacity in developing and least-developed countries. The contribution will support STDF activities that help countries meet international food safety and animal and plant health standards, as well as facilitate safe and inclusive trade.
topArticle.titleJa: アイルランド、開発途上国の貿易機会強化に20万ユーロを拠出
topArticle.summary: アイルランドは、開発途上国の貿易機会強化のため、STDFに20万ユーロを拠出します。

topArticle.title: Ethiopia's accession maintains momentum as WTO members review progress
topArticle.description: At its eighth meeting on 9 and 10 November, the Working Party on Ethiopia's Accession to the WTO took stock of the latest progress in bilateral market access negotiations and reforms of Ethiopia's foreign trade regime. Leading a high-level delegation, Ethiopia's Minister of Trade and Regional Integration and Chief Trade Negotiator, Yasmin Wohabrebbi Saeed, reaffirmed the priority the government continues to attach to achieving WTO accession as soon as possible. Members welcomed the progress achieved while noting that further work is needed before the accession process can be concluded.
topArticle.titleJa: エチオピアのWTO加盟、加盟国が進捗状況を審査し勢いを維持
topArticle.summary: エチオピアのWTO加盟作業部会は、市場アクセス交渉と貿易制度改革の進捗を確認しました。

topArticle.title: EU launches safeguard investigation on certain PET resin chemicals
topArticle.description: On 6 November 2026, the European Union notified the WTO’s Committee on Safeguards that it had initiated, on the same day (6 November 2026), a safeguard investigation on imports of certain polyethylene terephthalate resin chemicals.
